title: Lookup Table Refactoring: Towards Efficient Logarithmic Number System Addition for Large Language Models
problem: Logarithmic Number System addition requires complex nonlinear functions approximated via lookup tables, consuming significant hardware resources in LLM accelerators and limiting LNS adoption despite superior quantization alignment with long-tailed data distributions.
motivation: LNS quantization provides better precision than integer quantization for LLMs but impractical LUT resource consumption prevents deployment in area-constrained accelerators.
method: Analyzes LNS addition patterns specific to LLM workloads and derives mathematical relationships between LUT hardware parameters and computation error. Proposes LUT refactoring optimizing the LUT structure for LLM-specific operations while maintaining precision.
key_novelty: Hardware-aware LUT optimization explicitly targeting LNS operations in LLM multiply-accumulate pipelines.
contributions: Mathematical characterization of LUT-error trade-offs in LNS addition
LUT refactoring technique reducing area-delay product by 10.93% and power-delay product by 19.78%
33.5% accuracy improvement versus naive LNS design across benchmarks
18.27% area and 42.61% power reduction compared to integer quantization
limitations: Dynamic range limitations and applicability to different precision regimes not discussed.
